prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1374; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a collision in a parking lot. The insured driver is named on the policy, and the claimant is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the lawyer's office.

Entry 2: Police report places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the crash. Photos taken at the scene show the damage, and the vehicle damage is consistent with the impact described. No independent witness saw the collision itself.

Entry 3: Claimant reports a concussion from the impact. The injury fits the kind and force of a crash like this. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from prior records.

Entry 4: Initial account from the claimant is recorded and runs consistent with the police report. Some small details were added in a later conversation, but the core account has not changed.

Entry 5: A neighbor mentioned seeing the car with damage several weeks before the claimed loss date. This has not been confirmed, and I have asked for any repair or prior-damage records on the vehicle. None are known to exist so far.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a usual course, with follow-up visits tapering off as the claimant improved. The medical notes match the timeline of the reported symptoms.

Entry 7: Claim file reviewed with the supervisor. Liability and injury facts are being evaluated in light of the neighbor's comment, and the open item is obtaining any prior repair history for the vehicle before a decision is made.
